root_motivation: A tenant that already exists (an ICP row 1 agent owner, or synthorg's explore cohort standing in for one) points an OAuth client at its canonical resource `https://mcphost.dev/t/<ns>/mcp`. The client gets the correct 401 and fetches the tenant document, which says no authorization server exists. The client stops. synthorg's explore OAuth cohort fails 42 of 42 sessions a night this way (`explore-20261013T081050Z`, `sessions/admin_agent-11/session.json`: `oauth_trace = [{"step":"discover","status":"error"}]`), so the nightly read on OAuth clients has been zero information since the cohort shipped. The hosted authorization server would have issued a token for that very tenant: `resolve_resource_tenant` resolves the per-tenant resource to the tenant (`src/authz.rs:872-879`) and the token's `aud` is checked against the grant's recorded resource (`src/authz.rs:1920`). The document is wrong, not the server.
user_persona: An agent that calls host.state.delete_rows with an empty filter on a 5 000-row table, reads confirm_required.dry_run_first, runs the dry run, notices the empty filter and fixes it; a Claude Code user who sees a destructive marker on host.table.drop.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given tenant T with no issuers and no provider, When `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/t/<ns>/mcp` is called, Then `authorization_servers == ["<public_url>"]` and `resource == "<public_url>/t/<ns>/mcp"`.
Given T registered issuer I with `host.oauth.issuer_set`, When the tenant document is fetched, Then `authorization_servers == ["<public_url>", I]`; Given I equals `public_url`, Then it appears once.

Given `host.oauth.trusted_issuer_set` with issuer `toolconf-probe`, `ftp://x`, or `https://`, When called, Then the error code is `issuer_url_invalid` and no row is written; Given `https://idp.example.com` or `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, Then the row is written.

Given a stored issuer row whose value is `toolconf-probe`, When the root and the tenant documents are fetched, Then neither lists it and the process log carries one `issuer_url_invalid` warning naming the tenant id and count.

Given a fresh key-signup tenant on a test server, When the `oauthmeta` contract walk runs from its tenant document with no hard-coded authorization-server URL, Then `discover`, `metadata`, `register`, `authorize`, `consent`, and `token` succeed and a bearer `tools/call` on the document's `resource` returns the tenant's `host.whoami`.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod, When the tenant document for the joe-test tenant is fetched, Then its first authorization server is `https://mcphost.dev` (Live; evidence: `curl -s https://mcphost.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/t/t_3556946d/mcp | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["authorization_servers"][0])'`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- live: AC6 is a prod curl of the joe-test tenant document after deploy.

scope: src/confirm.rs (new): the gated set derived from WRITE_VERBS, token mint/hash, canonical args hash, confirm_required/confirm_invalid errors.
src/handler.rs: dispatch gate (dry-run measure, token check, scratch bypass), destructiveHint annotations and description suffix in host_tools.
non_goals: Human approval; gating scratch tenants; gating host.key.rotate and host.self.offboard; changing what any verb does once confirmed.

additional.token_never_stored: only sha256(token) is stored; the token is shown once by the dry run.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent delete 5 000 rows by accident?
five_whys_trace.a: dry_run is optional and nobody is required to read it.
Prose at a boundary is skipped; a refusal carrying the exact dry-run call cannot be.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bind the token to args and diff?
five_whys_trace.a: A token for another filter or another state would authorise a different delete.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which diffs are gated?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: A dry-run diff with a measurable row count (rows[].delete, tables[].rows) at or above plan confirm_rows_min; verbs that report no count are not gated yet.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Token bound to key or session?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Tenant (key hash), per the PRD default.
